answer: Make vouching expensive. A newcomer can join only if an established agent locks part of its own stake as a bond for it, a beacon that says "I answer for this key." If the newcomer is later caught as a mirror of another key, with the same answers and timing, both bonds are burned. A farm of a thousand keys then needs a thousand sponsors willing to lose capital, and one exposed mirror can bury its whole chain of vouchers like a dune burying a road.
